chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى الْعَلَاءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

chunks.arabic_text: فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ:

translations.en: Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Then write [a contract of emancipation] for them if you know good in them.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ "الْخَيْرُ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَ يَكُونَ بِيَدِهِ عَمَلٌ يَكْتَسِبُ بِهِ أَوْ يَكُونَ لَهُ حِرْفَةٌ".

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "The good is that he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that he has in his hand work by which he earns, or that he has a craft."

en.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic phrase about granting a contract of manumission to a slave when there is 'good' in him. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام interprets this good as sound faith and the practical ability to earn a livelihood through work or a craft.
en.seo_question: What does 'good' mean in the verse commanding a contract of emancipation in Surah al-Nūr 24:33?

key_terms.فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ: Grant them a mukātabah contract for emancipation
key_terms.خَيْرًا: Goodness here meaning faith and earning ability
key_terms.يَشْهَدَ: To bear witness to the testimony of faith
key_terms.عَمَلٌ: Work or labor through which one earns
key_terms.حِرْفَةٌ: A trade, craft, or vocational skill
